c.tagline: Where the Sava meets the Danube, and the party never quite stops.

taxi.fareNote: Use licensed companies (Pink Taxi, Beotaxi, Lux Taxi, Naxis) with visible taxi ID and working meter; airport transfers are often sold as a fixed price instead.

emergency.note: General EU-style emergency line 112 also works nationwide; fire brigade is 193.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Generally safe; usual pickpocket caution in the centre; football-match days can bring hooligan clashes

hood_desc: The historic old town packed with Kalemegdan Fortress, Knez Mihailova pedestrian street, and Skadarlija's bohemian taverns; best for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.
An upscale, leafy residential district anchored by the massive Church of Saint Sava, filled with cafes and boutiques; suits travelers wanting a quieter, local feel close to downtown.
A trendy riverside grid of low-rise buildings, specialty coffee shops, and Danube-side splav (raft club) nightlife; popular with younger travelers and digital nomads.
A fast-redeveloping riverside zone mixing gritty art squats with glossy new towers, malls, and the Sava promenade; good for travelers chasing nightlife and modern comforts.
A calmer former Habsburg-era fishing town on the Danube with cobbled lanes and the Gardoš Tower; ideal for travelers wanting a relaxed, authentic base away from downtown crowds.

water.note: Treated and generally safe, though a noticeable chlorine taste leads many visitors to prefer bottled water.

transit.pay: Buy a rechargeable contactless BusPlus card at kiosks/GSP outlets for the cheapest fares across bus, tram and trolleybus, or pay onboard with a single-ride SMS/driver ticket at a higher price. Many vehicles now also accept contactless bank-card tap-to-pay directly.
transit.hours: Most routes operate roughly 4:30/5:00 AM to 11:30 PM-midnight; a limited network of night lines (prefixed 'N') covers weekends into the early morning.
transit.note: Belgrade has no metro yet (a system is planned/under study); the BG Voz suburban rail supplements the bus/tram network on a few corridors.

bus: BAS Belgrade central bus station (intercity and international coaches)
ferry: Seasonal Sava/Danube river cruise and excursion boats

transit.m: A1 minibus shuttle to Slavija/city center (~40 min)
GSP city bus line 72 to Zeleni Venac (~45-50 min)

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving ~10% at restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory; for taxis, rounding to the nearest note is common.

food.name: Cevapi
food.desc: Small grilled skinless beef-and-lamb sausages served in warm lepinja flatbread with raw onion, kajmak and ajvar. Serbia's default everyday meal.

places.name: Sarajevski Cevap To Je To
places.note: Family-run Bosnian-style grill; the benchmark cevapi in the city, with kajmak and somun bread.

places.name: Cevap Kod Dekija
places.note: Cheap, generous portions a minute from Skadarlija; popular with locals late into the night.

places.name: Walter
places.note: Modern Sarajevo-style cevapdzinica with counter service and consistently high recent reviews.

food.name: Pljeskavica
food.desc: A wide, hand-formed grilled patty of mixed minced meat, often stuffed with kajmak or cheese and eaten in flatbread with onion and ajvar.

places.name: Tri Sesira
places.note: Open since 1864 in the bohemian quarter; grill classics with live tamburica music.

places.name: Durmitor
places.note: Meat-focused kafana known for huge grill platters and veal cooked under the sac.

places.name: Loki
places.note: Belgrade institution for oversized stuffed pljeskavica; queues at lunchtime.

food.name: Karadjordjeva snicla
food.desc: Rolled veal or pork schnitzel stuffed with kajmak, breaded and fried, served with tartar sauce. Nicknamed the maiden's dream.

places.name: Sesir Moj
places.note: Long-running Skadarlija kafana; textbook version with kajmak and roast potatoes.

places.name: Dva Jelena
places.note: Historic 1832 tavern serving old-school Serbian mains and live folk music nightly.

places.name: Tri Sesira
places.note: Reliable rendition on a menu of ajvar, kajmak and grill staples.

food.name: Burek
food.desc: Coiled filo pie of meat, cheese, spinach or potato, baked in huge round trays and cut by weight. Breakfast eaten with drinking yogurt.

places.name: Pekara Trpkovic
places.note: Nemanjina street bakery famous citywide; sells out of the meat burek by mid-morning.

places.name: Zeleni Venac market bakery
places.note: Market-corner pekara turning out enormous, properly greasy trays all morning.

places.name: Hleb i Kifle
places.note: Dependable 24-hour chain for late-night burek and yogurt near Republic Square.

food.name: Sarma and punjena paprika
food.desc: Minced meat and rice rolled in soured cabbage leaves or stuffed into peppers and slow-simmered with smoked meat; the classic Serbian home dish.

places.name: Znak Pitanja
places.note: Belgrade's oldest kafana, opposite the cathedral, cooking unchanged old-Serbian recipes.

places.name: Manufaktura
places.note: Umbrella-covered courtyard off Knez Mihailova; modernised Serbian home cooking.

places.name: Kafana SFRJ
places.note: Yugo-nostalgia kafana with hearty stews, sarma and a big rakija list.

food.name: Gibanica
food.desc: Layered filo pie of young white cheese and eggs, baked until puffed and golden. Eaten warm for breakfast or as a side to grilled meat.

places.name: Pekara Trpkovic
places.note: Bakes gibanica alongside its famous burek; go early for it hot from the tray.

places.name: Kafana SFRJ
places.note: Serves gibanica as a starter with kajmak, urnebes and pickles.

places.name: Manufaktura
places.note: Homemade version on a menu of Serbian classics in the central old town.

food.name: Rakija
food.desc: Serbia's national spirit, distilled from fruit; sljivovica from plums is the classic, with quince, apricot and honey-infused medovaca alongside.

places.name: Rakia Bar
places.note: Dedicated rakija bar with tasting flights across dozens of small Serbian distillers.

places.name: Kafana SFRJ
places.note: Deep house rakija selection poured by the glass with meze plates.

places.name: Sesir Moj
places.note: Traditional kafana pouring homemade sljivovica alongside live folk music.

food.name: Serbian beer and craft ale
food.desc: Jelen and Lav are the mainstream lagers, but Belgrade now has a strong craft scene using local plums, honey and hops from Vojvodina.

places.name: Kabinet Brewery taproom
places.note: One of Serbia's craft pioneers; rotating taps of local IPAs, sours and wheat beers.

places.name: Samo Pivo
places.note: Tiny, long-established beer bar with the widest Serbian craft list downtown.

places.name: Dogma Brewery
places.note: Warehouse-style taproom pouring experimental Serbian craft beer with bar snacks.

landmarks: Belgrade Fortress (Kalemegdan)
This monumental fortress complex overlooking the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers has guarded the city for two millennia and offers breathtaking sunset views.
Church of Saint Sava
One of the largest Orthodox churches in the world, its massive gold-domed silhouette dominates the Belgrade skyline and dazzles visitors with its marble interior.
Skadarlija
This cobblestoned bohemian quarter of cafes, street art, and live music evokes 19th-century Belgrade and is the city's favorite spot for atmospheric photos.
Republic Square
The bustling central square, framed by the National Museum and National Theatre, serves as Belgrade's meeting point and the symbolic heart of the city.
Nikola Tesla Museum
Home to the inventor's personal effects and interactive electrical demonstrations, this museum celebrates one of Serbia's most globally revered scientific minds.
Church of Saint Mark
Modeled after Serbia's medieval Gračanica monastery, this striking red-and-yellow brick church with Byzantine domes is a beloved architectural landmark near Tašmajdan Park.
House of the National Assembly
This grand early-20th-century parliament building with bronze statues and a domed roof stands as an emblem of Serbian democracy and neoclassical grandeur.
Ada Ciganlija
This river island turned urban beach and recreation hub on the Sava is where locals swim, cycle, and relax, offering a lively contrast to the historic center.
Gardoš Tower (Zemun)
This millennium-anniversary tower atop a hill in the riverside district of Zemun rewards climbers with sweeping views over the Danube and old town rooftops.
Knez Mihailova Street
Belgrade's grand pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century facades, boutiques, and street performers connects Republic Square to the fortress gates.

train.note: Long-distance trains use Beograd Centar (Prokop) station. The spectacular Bar line is currently Belgrade's only international train — a year-round sleeper plus a daytime train in summer. Trains to Budapest remain suspended for line works until at least mid-2026, and there are no trains to Zagreb, Sofia or Skopje — take the bus instead.

intl.to: Vienna, Budapest, Zurich, northern Italy & Montenegro

bus.note: International coaches use Belgrade's main bus station in Novi Beograd (Blok 42); buy tickets in advance in summer. For Sofia, buses are currently the only direct public transport.

ferry.note: Belgrade sits on the Danube far from the sea, so there are no scheduled passenger ferries — only multi-day river cruises call here.

full.name: Kragujevac

full.name: Čačak
full.blurb: Central Serbian town known for its riverside setting, orchards, and role in regional trade.

full.name: Niš
full.blurb: Ancient Balkan city known for its fortress, Roman roots, and lively student energy.
